title: Access and Procurement Journey Guide
author: Priya Raman
body:
Overview

This guide consolidates company-wide policies and operational procedures for access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, and travel. It is intended for requesters, approvers, and process owners. The procedures below balance speed, least-privilege, and auditability.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party service accounts.
- Excludes project-level transient experiments explicitly funded and documented by a product sponsor; such exceptions must be logged with legal and people-ops.

Key principles

- Least privilege: grant the minimum access required and set expirations where possible.
- Separation of duties: approvals should cross function (requester -> manager -> finance/security as applicable).
- Auditability: every access or procurement must have a ticket and cost center.
- Data classification: handle data according to classification (Public / Internal / Restricted / Regulated).

1) Access and Permissions lifecycle

Summary: standardized request -> justification -> owner approval -> provisioning -> periodic review.

Roles and responsibilities:

- Requester: initiates the request with justification and cost center.
- Manager: verifies business need and duration.
- Resource Owner (service or team owning the resource): approves technical scope and least-privilege mapping.
- Security (for Restricted/Regulated or cross-org access): performs a risk review.
- IT/Platform: performs provisioning and documents ticket.

Approval matrix (example):

| Resource type | Approval chain | Max duration without reapproval | Escalation owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| GitHub repo (read) | Manager -> Repo owner | 90 days | Eng Platform |
| Production database (read) | Manager -> Data owner -> Security | 30 days | Head of Security |
| Dedicated GPU cluster | Manager -> Infra cost owner -> Finance | 30 days | SRE lead |

Standard request flow (numbered):

1. Requester opens an Access Request ticket (Jira template: ACCESS-REQUEST) and selects resource and classification.
2. Include explicit justification, required TTL (time-to-live), and cost center code.
3. Manager approves in Jira; if approval is not provided within 48 hours, request auto-escalates to manager's manager.
4. Resource owner confirms mapping to least-privilege roles and approves.
5. IT/Platform performs provisioning and posts the provisioning record + checklist to the ticket.
6. On expiry, access is automatically revoked. Requests for extension require a new approval.

Temporary & emergency access

- Emergency access is permitted via the Emergency Access workflow (Jira tag: ACCESS-EMERGENCY).
- Emergency grants are time-limited (max 8 hours) and must be documented in the ticket with a postmortem within 72 hours.

Periodic review

- Quarterly entitlement sweep: owners must review active grants and close or re-scope stale entries.
- KPIs: 95% of grants have an expiry <= 90 days; 100% of production DB users reviewed monthly.

2) Change management (applies to infra, runtime, and data schemas)

Goals: prevent outages, enable rapid but safe changes, preserve rollback capability.

Change types and thresholds:

- Normal Change: non-prod schema tweaks, config-safe changes. Plan in CHG board and notify affected teams.
- High-Impact Change: production schema changes, runtime kernel upgrades, or infra replacements. Requires two approvers (owner + SRE) and a rollout window.
- Emergency Change: mitigations for P1/P0 incidents; follow emergency change process and complete post-change review.

Change submission checklist (short):

- Description of change, affected services, rollback plan, scheduled window, test plan, and owner.
- Impact analysis: latency/cost/availability and which customers are affected.
- Communication plan: status channel, pre/post messages, and runbook links.

Execution and rollback

1. Schedule change in the change calendar and create CHG ticket.
2. Notify stakeholders 72 hours before window for High-Impact; 24 hours for Normal.
3. Execute in the approved window; monitor predefined SLOs and business metrics.
4. If metrics cross thresholds (see SLOs table), trigger rollback and incident process.

SLO thresholds for automated rollback examples:

- API P50 latency > 2x baseline for >5 minutes -> rollback.
- Error rate > 0.5% for read APIs or >0.2% for write APIs for >3 minutes -> rollback.

3) Data management and classification

Classification model:

- Public: non-sensitive material (marketing collateral).
- Internal: operational data for day-to-day engineering and product work.
- Restricted: PIIs, internal strategy, or data requiring contractual controls.
- Regulated: data subject to compliance regimes (HIPAA, GDPR special category) and additional contractual controls.

Handling rules by class (brief):

- Public: no restrictions.
- Internal: stored in company storage with access controls; retained 3 years unless otherwise required.
- Restricted: encryption-at-rest and in transit mandatory; access only via approved IAM roles; must be cataloged.
- Regulated: additional contractual clauses; processing locations limited by region; subject to audits annually.

Data retention and deletion

- Default retention: 3 years for Internal, 7 years for business-critical financial records, as legal requires for Regulated.
- Data deletion requests follow the Data Deletion template (see Templates section).

4) Procurement and expenses

Procurement lifecycle (high-level):

1. Request: Initiator files a Purchase Request (PR) with justification, vendor, estimated COS, and cost center.
2. Manager approval: verifies budget and business need.
3. Procurement review (Finance procurement team): validates vendor onboarding status, commercial terms, and PII handling.
4. Contracting: Legal reviews terms for spend > $50k or any vendor storing Regulated data.
5. Purchase order & payment: Finance issues PO and processes invoice.

Approval thresholds (example):

- <$1,000: Manager approval.
- $1,000–$25,000: Manager + Finance reviewer.
- $25,000–$50,000: Manager + Procurement lead + Finance signoff.
- >$50,000: Manager + Procurement lead + Legal + Executive sponsor.

Card and expense policy highlights:

- Corporate card: for travel, subscriptions <= $2,000/yr, and low-value operational purchases.
- Personal reimbursement: itemized receipts required, submit within 30 days.
- Audit: Finance runs monthly card reconciliations and random expense audits quarterly.

Vendor onboarding & risk assessment

Checklist:

- Vendor contact and legal entity details.
- Data handling classification: does vendor process Restricted or Regulated data?
- Security review: evidence of SOC2 or equivalent for vendors with access to Internal/Restricted data.
- Contract terms: data processing addendum (DPA), liability caps, termination rights.
- Payment terms, PO requirements, and escalation contacts.

Vendor risk levels (summary):

- Low: SaaS tools with no Internal data access (no DPA).
- Medium: tools that store Internal data; require DPA and standard security checklist.
- High: vendors processing Restricted/Regulated data; require SOC2/ISO evidence, legal review, and quarterly security attestations.

5) Travel & out-of-region work

Booking and approvals:

- All business travel requires a Travel Request with estimated cost and safety assessment for the destination. Managers approve travel; trips with cost > $5k require finance review.
- Travelers must register high-risk trips with people-ops and complete any location-specific compliance training.

Expense reimbursements (high-level):

1. Submit expense via the Expense system with receipts and cost center.
2. Manager reviews and approves within 10 business days.
3. Finance processes reimbursements on the next payroll cycle if submitted by the cutoff.

Per diem and lodging rules:

- Per diem follows national guidelines for the travel country; lodging should use preferred suppliers when available.
- Upgrades (e.g., business class) require approval from an Executive sponsor for trips > 8 hours one-way.

6) Templates and artifacts (appendix)

Included templates (copy from Confluence template library):

- ACCESS-REQUEST (Jira template): fields - requester, resource, justification, TTL, cost center, classification.
- PURCHASE-REQ (Procurement form): fields - item, vendor, estimate, cost center, approver chain.
- DATA-DELETION-REQUEST (Form): fields - dataset id, reason, owner, retention exemption.
- TRAVEL-REG (Form): fields - itinerary, risk assessment, approver, emergency contact.

Example JSON snippet for a Purchase Request (for automation):

{
  "requester": "<name>",
  "vendor": "<vendor-name>",
  "estimated_amount_usd": "<amount>",
  "cost_center": "<code>",
  "data_classification": "Internal/Restricted/Regulated"
}

Governance & enforcement

- Policy exceptions must be documented and approved by people-ops + finance + legal (if applicable).
- Violations (misuse of cards, inappropriate access, or unapproved vendor data use) trigger an investigation and remedial actions which may include revocation of access or disciplinary steps.

Operational metrics to track (examples)

- Mean time to provision access (target < 48 hours).
- Percentage of access requests with explicit TTL (target 100%).
- Vendor onboarding cycle time (target < 15 business days for low/medium risk).
- Monthly travel expense reconciliation lag (target < 10 days).

Related resources and references

End of guide.
